The apparatus includes a semiconductor substrate on which a photoelectric conversion unit, a charge storage unit, and a floating diffusion unit are disposed. The photoelectric conversion unit is configured to receive incident light and generate charge corresponding to the received light. The charge storage unit is provided to temporarily store the charge generated by the photoelectric conversion unit, and the floating diffusion unit is configured to receive the stored charge and convert it into a voltage signal.

A first gate electrode is arranged between the photoelectric conversion unit and the charge storage unit. The apparatus further includes a light shielding member. The light shielding member has a first part disposed over the charge storage unit and over at least one of the first gate electrode and the second gate electrode. The light shielding member also has a second part extending from the first part toward the semiconductor substrate. The second part is located between the first gate electrode and the second gate electrode. By extending toward the semiconductor substrate in this region, the second part provides additional shielding between the gate electrodes, thereby suppressing light leakage toward the charge storage unit and improving charge retention and signal accuracy.
outputs.L4:
A solid-state image pickup apparatus includes a semiconductor substrate on which a plurality of functional regions are formed for capturing and processing image information. These regions include a photoelectric conversion unit that receives incident light and converts the light into electric charge, a charge storage unit that temporarily stores the generated charge, and a floating diffusion unit that receives the stored charge and converts it into a voltage signal. The apparatus also includes gate electrodes arranged on the semiconductor substrate to control the transfer of charge between these regions.

In this configuration, charge generated in the photoelectric conversion unit is transferred to the charge storage unit through operation of a gate electrode. The charge storage unit holds the charge until a predetermined readout timing, after which the charge is transferred to the floating diffusion unit through another gate electrode. The floating diffusion unit then produces an electrical signal corresponding to the amount of charge, enabling the apparatus to output image information.

To improve image quality, a light-shielding member is provided above the charge storage unit. This light-shielding member is arranged so as to block incident light from reaching the charge storage region, thereby preventing unwanted photoelectric conversion or the generation of unnecessary charge in that region. The light-shielding member is formed with a structure that extends downward between adjacent gate electrodes. This downward-extending section increases the shielding effect in an area where light might otherwise enter obliquely or leak through gaps between electrode structures.

By providing the downward-extending portion of the light-shielding member between the gate electrodes, the charge storage unit is more effectively protected from incident light. As a result, unwanted light-induced charge is reduced, and noise or false signals caused by light leakage are suppressed. This contributes to improved signal accuracy, reduced image artifacts, and better overall image quality in the solid-state image pickup apparatus.

Such a structure is particularly useful in image sensors in which charge must be stored temporarily before readout, because any unintended light entering the charge storage unit during the storage period can degrade the captured image. The improved light-shielding design helps maintain the integrity of the stored charge and enhances the performance and reliability of the image pickup apparatus.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. As a definite article, “the” helps us refer to something specific rather than something general. For example, saying “a book” could mean any book, while “the book” points to a particular one that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word adds clarity, precision, and structure to sentences. It guides readers and listeners by showing that a noun is known, unique, or already mentioned. We use “the” when talking about famous places, such as “the Eiffel Tower,” natural features like “the ocean,” and objects or ideas that are clearly identified in context.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” is essential to fluent English. Without it, sentences can sound incomplete or unnatural. Its frequent use shows how even the smallest words can have a powerful effect on meaning. In writing and speech, “the” helps turn general ideas into specific ones, making communication clearer and more effective.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical description in patent language for a CMOS solid-state imaging device where a light shielding member is placed over a charge storage unit and at least one adjacent gate electrode, with another portion extending between first and second gate electrodes.
counterfactuals.output:
A CMOS solid-state imaging device includes a semiconductor substrate having a plurality of pixels arranged in a pixel array. Each pixel includes a photoelectric conversion element configured to generate signal charge in response to incident light, a charge storage unit configured to temporarily store the signal charge transferred from the photoelectric conversion element, and a plurality of gate electrodes formed over the semiconductor substrate for controlling transfer and readout of the signal charge.

In one embodiment, the plurality of gate electrodes includes a first gate electrode and a second gate electrode disposed adjacent to one another with an intervening spacing therebetween. The charge storage unit may be formed in an impurity region of the semiconductor substrate and may be disposed adjacent to at least one of the first and second gate electrodes. For example, the charge storage unit may constitute a floating diffusion region, a memory node, or another charge accumulation region used for holding charge prior to conversion into a voltage signal.

A light shielding member is provided above the semiconductor substrate so as to suppress incidence of undesired light onto the charge storage unit. The light shielding member is disposed at least over the charge storage unit and over at least one gate electrode adjacent to the charge storage unit. In particular, the light shielding member may overlap, in plan view, the charge storage unit and a portion of the first gate electrode or the second gate electrode. By covering both the charge storage unit and the adjacent gate electrode, the light shielding member reduces generation of parasitic charge in the charge storage unit and suppresses optical leakage paths near the gate edge region.

The light shielding member further includes an extending portion arranged to extend into a region between the first gate electrode and the second gate electrode. The extending portion is positioned in the inter-gate spacing and may extend downwardly or laterally between the gate electrodes through an insulating layer formed over the semiconductor substrate. In plan view, the extending portion may be arranged so as to at least partially overlap the gap between the first and second gate electrodes. The extending portion blocks obliquely incident light that might otherwise pass through the inter-gate spacing and reach the charge storage unit or an adjacent semiconductor region.

The light shielding member may be formed of a metal material, a metal compound, polysilicon, tungsten, aluminum, copper, titanium nitride, or another opaque conductive or nonconductive material. The light shielding member may be electrically floating or may be connected to a predetermined potential, such as a ground potential or a fixed bias potential, depending on the device configuration. An insulating film may be interposed between the light shielding member and the gate electrodes to electrically isolate the light shielding member from the gate electrodes.

The first and second gate electrodes may include, for example, a transfer gate for transferring charge from the photoelectric conversion element to the charge storage unit, a reset gate for resetting the charge storage unit, or another transistor gate used in a pixel readout circuit. The portion of the light shielding member extending between the first and second gate electrodes may be arranged so as not to interfere with operation of the gate electrodes while increasing optical shielding efficiency in a region where light is otherwise likely to enter due to spacing between the electrodes.

Accordingly, the CMOS solid-state imaging device suppresses light-induced noise and dark-current-like signal components caused by unwanted photoelectric conversion at or near the charge storage unit. In particular, shielding the charge storage unit, shielding an adjacent gate electrode, and providing an inter-gate extending portion between the first and second gate electrodes improve charge retention accuracy and reduce image artifacts such as smear, blooming, and false signal generation. The configuration is especially advantageous in pixels having a temporary charge storage region or global shutter memory node, where undesired light exposure during a charge holding period can degrade image quality.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for a solid-state image pickup apparatus comprising a photodiode, memory node, floating diffusion, first and second gate electrodes, and a light shield configured to suppress light leakage into the charge storage unit.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention is provided for a solid-state image pickup apparatus, such as a CMOS image sensor, capable of reducing photoelectric-charge noise caused by light leakage into a charge storage unit.

The apparatus includes a semiconductor substrate in which a photodiode is formed. The photodiode serves as a photoelectric conversion unit that receives incident light and generates signal charge corresponding to the amount of received light. Adjacent to the photodiode, a memory node is provided as a charge storage unit for temporarily storing the signal charge generated by the photodiode. A floating diffusion region is also formed in the substrate and functions as a charge-to-voltage conversion node for converting transferred signal charge into an electrical voltage signal.

A first gate electrode is disposed between the photodiode and the memory node. By applying a control voltage to the first gate electrode, signal charge accumulated in the photodiode can be transferred to the memory node. A second gate electrode is disposed between the memory node and the floating diffusion. By controlling the second gate electrode, the charge stored in the memory node can be transferred to the floating diffusion for readout.

The apparatus further includes a light shield formed above at least the memory node, and preferably above the memory node and portions of the transfer gate regions. The light shield is made of a light-blocking material, such as tungsten, aluminum, copper, or another opaque conductive or metallic material, and is arranged so as to prevent incident light from reaching the memory node. The light shield may be formed in an interlayer insulating film above the semiconductor substrate and may overlap the memory node in plan view.

By shielding the memory node from incident light, the invention suppresses generation of unwanted charge in or near the charge storage unit. This reduces light leakage, parasitic sensitivity, smear, and noise during charge storage, particularly in global-shutter image sensors where charge is temporarily held in the memory node before readout. As a result, the apparatus improves image quality and enables accurate signal readout even under strong illumination.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
